issues.description: Entire compiled script loaded into RPC payload and React state with no size bound
issues.detail: The backend reads the entire compiled .kale.py file into memory and returns it inline in the RPC response, and the frontend then carries it in component state until the user clicks Download. There is no stated bound on script size; for large notebooks the compiled artifact can be hundreds of KB to several MB, and it traverses the RPC channel and lives in React state for every queued deploy. Asymptotically this is O(n) per compile where n = script size, but the constants (JSON-encode, base64/transport overhead, retained-in-state duplication) are substantial. A streaming endpoint that serves the file on demand (GET /download?path=...) would be O(1) in memory until requested and would not pay the cost on every compile.

issues.description: No invariant or termination reasoning on script_path read; missing encoding and error handling
issues.detail: open(script_path) is called without an explicit encoding (relies on locale default, which is not portable) and without handling FileNotFoundError or IOError. The invariant the author seems to assume is 'compile_pipeline always leaves script_path readable on disk' but this is not stated, and on failure paths the RPC will raise an uncaught OSError instead of the structured error the rest of compile_notebook returns. State the invariant in a comment and either assert it or handle the violation explicitly.

issues.description: Filename fallback 'pipeline.kale.py' can mask a real bug rather than expose it
issues.detail: fileName = props.compiledPath.split('/').pop() || 'pipeline.kale.py' silently substitutes a default when compiledPath is the empty string. Since the surrounding branch is gated on props.compiledPath && props.compiledContent, the fallback is unreachable in correct operation; if it ever fires, it hides the inconsistency. Prefer asserting the invariant (compiledPath is non-empty here) or logging, rather than producing a plausible-looking but wrong filename.

issues.description: Download click handler lacks a literate comment explaining the blob-anchor dance
issues.detail: The createObjectURL / anchor / click / revokeObjectURL sequence is a well-known browser idiom but it is not obvious to a reader who has not seen it. A 2-3 line comment stating the invariant ('we synthesize a transient object URL, click a detached anchor to trigger the browser download UI, then release the URL') would make the function readable without running it. This is exactly the kind of place literate commentary pays off because the code looks like it is doing five unrelated DOM operations.

issues.description: GetAppIcon used as a button is not keyboard-accessible and lacks semantic role
issues.detail: The download trigger is an <GetAppIcon onClick=...> styled with cursor:pointer. titleAccess gives it an accessible name, but it is not focusable, has no role='button', and cannot be activated by Enter/Space. A serious reader of this UI code would want either an IconButton or an <a download> wrapper. This is a small change with disproportionate readability and correctness gain.

issues.description: Data could be carried by reference (path) rather than by value (full content)
issues.detail: The right data structure here is arguably a handle (the existing compiledPath) plus a download endpoint, not the file contents copied through three layers (Python -> RPC -> Commands -> DeploysProgress state -> DeployProgress props). The current design pays O(n) memory at every layer for an event that happens once on click, if at all. Pike's 'data structures, not algorithms' applies: pick the cheaper representation.

review.summary: The feature is small and the algorithm (read file, ship bytes, synthesize a download) is trivially correct, but the data-structure choice is the wrong one: the full compiled script is copied by value through the RPC and held in React state on every compile, when a handle-plus-endpoint would be O(1) until the user actually clicks. The backend read is also under-audited: no encoding, no error handling, no stated invariant about when script_path is guaranteed readable. The frontend click handler is correct but unreadable without a literate comment explaining the blob/anchor idiom, and the icon-as-button pattern is not keyboard-accessible. Verdict: UNDER-AUDITED and WRONG-DATA-STRUCTURE; ship-worthy after bounding the payload (or switching to a download endpoint) and tightening the backend read.
